opening_message:
Ticket 1: Alyssa Rose (employee ID E026) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E026.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Employee is full-time Analyst. Requested write to Payroll; full-time employees can have up to write (admin only if role owns the system). Grant write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E026 is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors with basic training max out at read (write requires advanced training). Requested write exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: The two notes conflict on employment type: HR reports full_time (max write), while Security reports contractor with basic security training. Per policy, contractors max out at read unless they have advanced security training, and the Security note confirms basic training. Since the employee's verified contractor status gives a maximum of read, the requested write exceeds the maximum, so I grant the maximum permitted level: read. (Role Analyst does not own Payroll, so admin is not applicable either way.)
